Compare Medical Decision Tests

Source: R/decisioncompare.h.R
decisioncompare.Rd

Function for comparing multiple Medical Decision Tests. Compares sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and other metrics between different tests against the same gold standard. Includes statistical comparison using McNemar's test and confidence intervals for differences. Tests are paired within each case; cases must be independent across rows. Repeated specimens or lesions from one patient require a method that accounts for clustering. Explicit positive and negative levels are required for the reference and every selected test. Other observed levels require explicit exclusion or prior recoding; they are never pooled as negative.

Usage

decisioncompare(
  data,
  referenceType = "legacy",
  referenceDescription = "",
  targetDefinition = "",
  gold = NULL,
  goldPositive,
  goldNegative,
  test1 = NULL,
  test1Positive,
  test1Negative,
  test2 = NULL,
  test2Positive,
  test2Negative,
  test3 = NULL,
  test3Positive,
  test3Negative,
  pp = FALSE,
  pprob = 0.3,
  od = FALSE,
  fnote = FALSE,
  ci = FALSE,
  plot = FALSE,
  excludeIndeterminate = FALSE,
  radarplot = FALSE,
  heatmap = FALSE,
  opa = FALSE,
  niMargin = 75,
  useOpaCriterion = FALSE,
  ciMethod = "wilson",
  stratify = NULL,
  statComp = FALSE,
  mcnemarMethod = "midp",
  showSummary = FALSE,
  showExplanations = FALSE,
  showReportSentence = FALSE,
  showDescriptiveReport = FALSE,
  showValidationContext = FALSE,
  cohortRole = "",
  samplingDesign = "",
  thresholdSource = "",
  modelVersion = "",
  analysisUnit = ""
)

Arguments

data

The data as a data frame.

referenceType

Comparator interpretation; legacy retains diagnostic terminology. All modes require explicit positive and negative levels. Consensus and method report agreement without disease-risk interpretation.

referenceDescription

Free text describing the reference or comparator (e.g. consensus of three pathologists); displayed in the Reference and target table and, when shown, the Validation context table; not validated.

targetDefinition

Free text defining the target condition the positive level represents; displayed in the Reference and target table only, not validated.

gold

The reference variable; its interpretation is selected separately.

goldPositive

The positive reference level; disease interpretation requires a disease standard.

goldNegative

Explicit negative level, required for each selected variable. Pass NULL only when this variable is not selected.

test1

The first diagnostic test variable being evaluated for performance.

test1Positive

The level representing a positive result for Test 1.

test1Negative

Explicit negative level, required for each selected variable. Pass NULL only when this variable is not selected.

test2

The second diagnostic test variable for comparison analysis.

test2Positive

The level representing a positive result for Test 2.

test2Negative

Explicit negative level, required for each selected variable. Pass NULL only when this variable is not selected.

test3

Optional third diagnostic test variable for extended comparison analysis.

test3Positive

The level representing a positive result for Test 3.

test3Negative

Explicit negative level, required for each selected variable. Pass NULL only when this variable is not selected.

pp

Enable custom prior probability (prevalence) for predictive value calculations.

pprob

Prior probability (disease prevalence in the community). Requires a value strictly between 0 and 1, default 0.300.

od

Boolean selection whether to show frequency tables. Default is 'false'.

fnote

Boolean indicating whether table footnotes should be displayed.

ci

Boolean indicating whether confidence interval tables should be displayed.

plot

Generate comparison plot showing test performance metrics.

excludeIndeterminate

If TRUE, exclude results outside the explicit positive/negative pairs. If FALSE, additional observed levels cause a validation error. Both levels are always required; neither missing mappings nor extra labels invoke one-versus-rest recoding.

radarplot

Generate radar plot for comprehensive test comparison visualization.

heatmap

Generate concordance heatmap comparing per-case test results against gold standard.

opa

Show overall percent agreement with 95 percent confidence intervals for each test.

niMargin

Minimum acceptable OPA percentage (default 75). Retains the niMargin option name for compatibility with saved analyses.

useOpaCriterion

Whether to apply the descriptive minimum OPA criterion.

ciMethod

CI method for overall percent agreement: wilson (default), logit, or exact (Clopper-Pearson). Logit falls back to Clopper-Pearson at 0 or 100 percent agreement.

stratify

Optional stratification variable for subgroup-specific diagnostic accuracy analysis.

statComp

Perform statistical comparison between tests (McNemar's test and confidence intervals for differences).

mcnemarMethod

McNemar test for the pairwise comparisons: midp (default; Fagerland et al. 2013) or asymptotic (chi-squared without continuity correction).

showSummary

Boolean to show natural language summary of statistical comparisons.

showExplanations

Boolean to show explanations, glossary, and educational content.

showReportSentence

Boolean to show manuscript-ready report sentence.

showDescriptiveReport

Boolean to show the longer descriptive report templates.

showValidationContext

Display the user-declared validation context (cohort role, sampling design, threshold source, model version, unit of observation) with the reference interpretation and comparator description in the Validation context table.

cohortRole

Declared role of this cohort (e.g. development, internal or external validation); displayed only, not verified.

samplingDesign

Declared sampling design (e.g. consecutive, case-control); displayed only, not verified. Case-control sampling distorts predictive values.

thresholdSource

Declared origin of any cut-off used to make the tests binary (e.g. prespecified, chosen in this sample); displayed only, not verified.

modelVersion

Declared version of the test, assay or algorithm; displayed only, not verified.

analysisUnit

Declared unit each row represents (e.g. case, patient, lesion); displayed only, not verified. This analysis assumes independent rows.

Value

A results object containing:

results$noticesa html
results$levelMappinga table
results$goldFrequencya table
results$originalCrossTaba table
results$cTable1a table
results$epirTable1a table
results$cTable2a table
results$epirTable2a table
results$cTable3a table
results$epirTable3a table
results$comparisonTablea table
results$opaTablea table
results$stratifiedTablea table
results$mcnemarTablea table
results$diffTablea table
results$plot1an image
results$plotRadaran image
results$plotHeatmapan image
results$summaryReporta html
results$reportSentencea html
results$explanationsContenta html
results$clinicalReporta html
results$aboutAnalysisa html
results$referenceDefinitiona table
results$comparatorCountsa table
results$comparatorPopulationa table
results$comparatorMetricsa table
results$comparatorReporta html
results$comparatorDifferencesa table
results$comparatorStrataa table
results$comparatorPlotan image
results$comparatorRadaran image
results$comparatorHeatmapan image
results$validationContexta table

Tables can be converted to data frames with asDF or as.data.frame. For example:

results$levelMapping$asDF

as.data.frame(results$levelMapping)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Level arguments are explicit in the generated R API. Pass NULL for
# the unused optional third test selectors only.
decisioncompare(
    data = histopathology,
    gold = "Golden Standart",
    goldPositive = "1",
    goldNegative = "0",
    test1 = "New Test",
    test1Positive = "1",
    test1Negative = "0",
    test2 = "Rater 1",
    test2Positive = "1",
    test2Negative = "0",
    test3 = NULL,
    test3Positive = NULL,
    test3Negative = NULL,
    statComp = TRUE
)
} # }
